Abstract The synergy between laboratory testing and numerical analysis represents a key frontier in the field of fracture mechanics. In this work, we investigate a numerical–experimental comparison for a dog-bone specimen featuring non-aligned pre-notches, made of an EN AW-6060 aluminum alloy exhibiting ductile fracture behavior. The central idea of this study is to demonstrate that a brittle fracture phase-field model, specifically, a fourth-order AT2 formulation, can provide physically meaningful and conservative predictions when applied to a ductile fracture problem, without explicitly accounting for plastic dissipation. The study aims to achieve both qualitative (crack pattern) and quantitative (peak reaction force) agreement between experiments and simulations, while assessing the influence of key phase-field parameters, including fracture toughness and internal length, on the overall response. The results show that the brittle model yields peak load predictions within 3.5% of the experimental measurements and successfully reproduces the experimentally observed crack patterns, supporting its use as a conservative design tool in engineering applications Published: 2026-09-08T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Unknown 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考

This study proposes an experiment-efficient ANN-based framework for characterizing the anisotropy of AA6022-T4 and calibrating the Yld2004-18p anisotropic yield function from a single hole expansion (HE) test and evaluates its predictions against two texture-driven meso-scale plasticity approaches, namely crystal plasticity finite element method (CPFEM) and elasto-visco-plastic self-consistent (ΔEVPSC). The ANN framework exploits the heterogeneous deformation field generated during the HE test, with training data obtained from finite element (FE) simulations using randomly assigned Yld2004-18p parameters. Two distinct ANN frameworks are developed: one predicts anisotropic properties (stress ratios and r-values), while the other directly estimates Yld2004-18p parameters. Three ANN input selection strategies are explored, i.e., using all strain components from 21 extraction locations in the HE simulation, local stress-based selection, and a variance-based approach. In the crystal plasticity approaches, CPFEM and ΔEVPSC simulations based solely on the measured initial crystallographic texture provide virtual uniaxial and equibiaxial responses that are subsequently fitted to Yld2004-18p. Comparative assessment shows that the ANN framework, as well as the CPFEM- and ΔEVPSC-based approaches, reproduces the anisotropic response, yield locus, and HE thinning profile of the material with generally good agreement with experiments and with the conventional calibration, while substantially reducing experimental time, cost, and material consumption. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E5%8F%82%E6%95%B0%E6%A0%87%E5%AE%9A%E4%B8%8E%E5%8F%8D%E6%BC%94+%E6%92%A4%E9%94%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v1+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.3390%2Fmet16091030%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22reset%22%2C+%22scope%22%3A+%22calibration%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22calibration%22%5D%7D%0A%60%60%60 Accurate identification of constitutive parameters is essential for reliable finite element simulations of sheet metal forming processes. Conventional inverse identification techniques, such as Finite Element Model Updating (FEMU), generally require iterative optimization procedures involving numerous finite element simulations, resulting in high computational cost. This work proposes a machine learning framework based on a bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) neural network for the identification of combined isotropic–kinematic hardening parameters from a custom-designed reverse bending test. A synthetic dataset comprising 5000 finite element simulations was generated by systematically varying the parameters of the Swift isotropic hardening law and the Armstrong–Frederick kinematic hardening law using Sobol sampling. The resulting force–displacement histories were used to train the Bi-LSTM network to predict five constitutive parameters (K, σ0, n, C, and γ) directly from force–displacement responses. To improve the physical admissibility of the predictions, a physically constrained loss function was introduced by penalizing negative values of the kinematic hardening parameters during training. The proposed model achieved coefficients of determination, R2 above 0.98 for the isotropic and kinematic hardening parameters while reducing the number of physically inadmissible predictions from approximately 30 to a single case. Experimental validation was performed on DP500 and DP780 advanced high-strength steels, where finite element simulations using the Bi-LSTM predicted parameters reproduced the experimentally measured springback angles with good agreement. The proposed methodology provides near-instantaneous constitutive parameter identification after training, eliminating the need for computationally expensive iterative optimization while maintaining high predictive accuracy and physical consistency. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E5%A1%91%E6%80%A7%E5%8F%98%E5%BD%A2%E4%B8%8E%E7%A1%AC%E5%8C%96%E5%BE%8B+%E6%92%A4%E9%94%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v1+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.ijsolstr.2026.114289%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22reset%22%2C+%22scope%22%3A+%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%7D%0A%60%60%60 In this work, a new methodology for the identification of sheet metal constitutive model parameters is presented. This methodology is based on the application of Machine Learning models, in conjunction with the Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm, and was applied to the identification of the Swift hardening law and the CPB06 yield criterion parameters. The proposed methodology uses data obtained from the results of a cruciform biaxial tensile test and aims to overcome some of the challenges inherent to the characterization of materials with the CPB06 yield criterion. The predictive performances obtained were satisfactory overall, when comparing both the stress–strain curves and the yield surfaces obtained for the testing materials, highlighting the potential of the proposed methodology. Abstract Thrombus fragmentation during mechanical thrombectomy may lead to distal embolization, yet its fracture mechanism remains difficult to predict because thrombi undergo large deformation, fiber-network rearrangement, and composition-dependent mechanical responses. This study aims to develop a continuum fracture framework for analyzing thrombus crack initiation and propagation while accounting for evolving fibrin-network anisotropy. A finite-deformation anisotropic phase-field fracture model is formulated by coupling a hyperelastic matrix response, fiber-induced anisotropic reinforcement, composition-dependent constitutive scaling, damage degradation, and a stretch-driven fiber-reorientation law. The main innovation is to treat the preferred fibrin direction as an evolving internal structural variable that reorients toward the local maximum-principal-stretch direction and influences the anisotropic stored energy and crack-driving history field. The model is implemented in abaqus through a staggered user-defined material–user-defined element procedure. The constitutive parameters are calibrated using fibrin-gel tensile data, and the fracture response is compared with notched uniaxial fracture experiments using experimentally motivated fracture toughness values. Additional numerical parametric studies are performed to examine the effects of fiber dispersion, reorientation parameters, and loading configuration on fracture behavior. The results indicate that fiber reorientation and dispersion can markedly affect the force–displacement response, damage localization, and crack-propagation path. The proposed framework provides a basis for studying thrombus fracture under large deformation and may support future model extensions involving fluid migration, vessel confinement, and clot–device interaction. item.title: Quasi in-situ analysis of twinning evolution in AZ31 magnesium alloy under different dynamic compression strain rates
item.description: 库内相似论文：Mechanical behavior and microstructure evolution of a rolled magnesium alloy AZ31B under low stress triaxiality（相似度 0.824） 应变率效应: 可作为率项形式、率敏感性转折和动态试验技术的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对率区间、波形是否平衡、是否与准静态同一试样构型 仅题名片段: Quasi in-situ analysis of twinning evolution … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 其他金属的同链研究: 研究链一致时与钛合金同等参考价值；建模思路、标定流程与验证方案可直接借鉴（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对材料体系差异与微观机制是否可比；参数量级不可直接套用，需在 TC4 上重新标定 仅题名片段: Quasi in-situ analysis of twinning evolution … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 公开阅读反馈 直接有用: Constitutive models are fundamental to solid mechanics and materials science, underpinning the quantitative description of material behaviors. Traditional phenomenological models are often built on expert intuition and empirical fitting, which limits their generalizability. In this work, we propose a graph-based equation discovery framework for automated discovery of constitutive laws directly from multicase experimental data. This framework expresses equations as directed graphs, where nodes represent operators and variables, edges denote computational relations, and edge features encode parametric dependencies. This enables the generation and optimization of free-form symbolic expressions with undetermined material-specific parameters. Through the framework, we have found constitutive models for strain-rate effects in alloy steel materials, deformation behavior of lithium metal, and hyperelastic behavior of filled rubbers. The discovered models exhibit compact analytical structures and achieve higher accuracy than empirical models. The proposed framework provides a generalizable and interpretable approach for data-driven scientific modeling, particularly in contexts where traditional empirical models are inadequate for representing complex physical phenomena. Despite their great potential for lightweight impact protection, the yield behavior of lattice materials under general stress states is complicated by factors such as loading orientation, hydrostatic stress, and strain rate, and a unified description has yet to be developed. Also, initial yield strength was commonly used to describe the yield surface of materials; however, it may be inaccurate for lattice materials and other cellular-based materials because of the presence of geometric nonlinearities (e.g., local strut buckling) and stochastic imperfections in manufacturing (like cell-wall thickness variations and nodal connectivity defects). Therefore, this work investigated the rate-dependent yielding and post-yield deformation behavior of lattice materials under dynamic loading. Body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice materials with four orientation angles (α = 0°, 15°, 30°, and 45°) were printed using 316L stainless steel. Quasi-static and dynamic compression tests were conducted, and finite element (FE) models were established and validated. During the long-stroke deformation of lattice materials, plateau stress reflects the steady-state performance of the whole sample and would be a more reliable metric for lattice's effective "yield strength" than a transient initial peak. Therefore, plateau stress was employed as the characteristic strength for yield-surface construction. The Hill 48 yield formulation was generalized by incorporating hydrostatic stress dependence and strain-rate sensitivity of plateau strength over a wide loading-rate range. Further, the post-yield collapse deformation and energy absorption of lattice materials were analyzed. The proposed model is able to capture the orientation-dependent collapse behavior and rate-induced strengthening while preserving a consistent yield-surface shape. The results elucidate the connection between hydrostatic-sensitive, rate-dependent yielding and energy absorption, providing guidance for the design of lattice materials with tailored performance. The article deals with the effect of stress triaxiality on the inelastic deformation behavior of aluminum alloys. The proposed continuum model takes into account stress triaxiality dependence of the yield condition as well as of the damage criterion and the fracture condition with different branches corresponding to various damage and failure modes depending on the stress triaxiality and the Lode parameter. Results of numerical cell simulations on the microscale are presented and corresponding identification of micromechanically motivated material parameters is discussed. Furthermore, numerical results of three-dimensional macromechanical finite element analyses are compared with experimental data obtained from smooth and pre-notched tension specimens. The analyses allow verification of the continuum model and identification of further material parameters. The single-distance phase retrieval technique was applied to contrast-enhanced imaging of the dual-phase microstructure of a ferrite/martensite dual-phase with only 1.4% difference in density between the two phases. Each high-resolution absorption-contrast image was registered with a corresponding phase-contrast image, to analyse damage evolution behaviour. The loading step at which each microvoid was nucleated was identified by tracking the microvoid throughout tension, together with its nucleation site. Premature damage initiation was observed at a relatively early stage at various nucleation sites, such as the ferrite interior, martensitic interior and ferrite/martensite interfaces; however, the subsequent growth of such microvoids was relatively moderate. On the other hand, microvoids were also initiated later due to martensitic cracking after the maximum load was reached, and these microvoids subsequently exhibited rapid growth. The martensite cracking induced additional damage evolution mainly along nearby ferrite/martensite interfaces and intersections between the martensite and the ferrite grain boundary. It is notable that the microvoids originating from martensitic cracking exhibited characteristic shear-dominated growth under macroscopic tension, whereas those originating from the other nucleation sites exhibited traditional triaxiality-dominated growth. It was concluded that the ductile fracture was dominated by the substantial force driving the growth of microvoids located on morphologically characteristic martensitic particles.
